trigger: irreversible-operations (npm publish to the public latest dist-tag)
summary: 6 substantiated doubts, no hard blocker. Sound: fork/PR-opener cannot trigger (write access needed to push a tag); tag<->version guard is correct; OIDC fails closed with no trusted-publisher config; --access public defaults to the latest dist-tag as intended. HIGH (latest-race) and one MEDIUM (prerelease->latest) FIXED in the workflow; a second MEDIUM (no pre-publish verify) FIXED; 2 LOW accepted in writing, 1 LOW (late-403) FIXED. YAML re-validated, ci-action-pinning-posture 10/10 re-pass, ci_supplychain_ack re-recorded (fingerprint 7a81007153).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: concurrency group publish-npm-${{ github.ref }} is UNIQUE per tag, so v0.25.0 and v0.26.0 pushed close together do NOT serialize; both npm publish set the latest dist-tag and the LAST to finish wins, so latest could land on the OLDER version.
doubts.disproof_attempt: FIXED - changed to a FIXED group 'publish-npm' (not keyed on the ref) with cancel-in-progress:false, so all publishes serialize and a queued one still runs. Header comment corrected.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: See disproof_attempt (FIXED in the workflow, or ACCEPTED in writing in the header + ack).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The tag<->version guard does not reject a prerelease; a v0.26.0-next.1 tag with a matching package.json would publish straight to the latest dist-tag, bypassing the documented @next channel.
doubts.disproof_attempt: FIXED - the guard now rejects any version containing '-' (prerelease) with a clear message pointing at the manual @next flow. This workflow is stable-latest-only by contract.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: See disproof_attempt (FIXED in the workflow, or ACCEPTED in writing in the header + ack).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: No pre-publish verification before the irreversible npm publish; a build that succeeds but produces an empty/broken dist would burn a version number.
doubts.disproof_attempt: FIXED - added a 'Verify built artifact before publish' step: assert server/dist/index.js and client/dist/index.html are non-empty and npm pack --dry-run assembles the tarball, before publish.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: See disproof_attempt (FIXED in the workflow, or ACCEPTED in writing in the header + ack).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: id-token:write is present while npm ci runs dependency install scripts, so a compromised transitive install script could mint an OIDC publish token.
doubts.disproof_attempt: ACCEPTED in writing (documented in the workflow header + ack). Inherent to Actions + native deps; blast radius bounded by an infrequent, write-gated, manual release. Splitting build/publish into two jobs would tighten it if ever judged worth the complexity.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: See disproof_attempt (FIXED in the workflow, or ACCEPTED in writing in the header + ack).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: Git tags are not branch-protected, so a maintainer can tag any commit and tag-push authority equals release authority.
doubts.disproof_attempt: ACCEPTED in writing. Cutting the tag IS the human gate by design; an optional 'environment: npm-publish' approval gate is documented (commented) for a second gate.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: See disproof_attempt (FIXED in the workflow, or ACCEPTED in writing in the header + ack).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: A re-pushed or already-published version 403s late, at the publish step, after a full build.
doubts.disproof_attempt: FIXED - the guard now runs npm view early and fails fast with a clear 'already published, bump and re-tag' message before the build. (Also means re-pushing the manually-published v0.25.0 tag would fail fast rather than confusingly late.)
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: See disproof_attempt (FIXED in the workflow, or ACCEPTED in writing in the header + ack).
